Recent featured work

Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series · 2026

First author

A reaction network,
learned as a graph.

NuGNN follows the connections between isotopes and nuclear reactions to predict changes in composition. The model accurately reproduces final abundance patterns when used in network evolution calculations.

Explore the NuGNN paper

Physical Review C · 2026

First author

Nuclear masses,
beyond the measured region.

Domain-informed (physics-informed) activation functions bring physical structure into a neural network, improving nuclear mass extrapolation beyond the training region.

Explore the DAF paper

Physical Review C · 2024

First author

From scattering data
to nuclear resonances.

Probabilistic neural networks infer resonance parameters from scattering data with quantified uncertainties. The framework combines a phenomenological R-matrix model with deep ensembles.

Explore the R-matrix paper

Deep learning & nuclear astrophysics

NuGNN: A Graph Neural Network for Nuclear Reaction Network Equations

C. H. Kim et al. · The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series 287, 34 (2026)

A graph neural network surrogate for the evolution of a 690-isotope nuclear reaction network.

Research summary by AI +

NuGNN represents isotopes and reactions as distinct node types and follows their physical connections through message passing. When integrated into a network evolution code, it reproduces final abundance patterns for Type I X-ray burst trajectories.

Deep learning & nuclear structure

Robust extrapolation in nuclear mass predictions using domain-informed activation functions

C. H. Kim et al. · Physical Review C 113, 024308 (2026)

Bringing nuclear physics into neural networks to improve predictions beyond measured masses.

Research summary by AI +

This study replaces conventional activation functions with domain-informed functions and uses sparse learning to reduce model complexity. Extrapolation is evaluated on outermost measured nuclei while training only on the inner region of the nuclear landscape.

Uncertainty quantification & nuclear reactions

Probabilistic neural networks for improved analyses with phenomenological R-matrix

C. H. Kim et al. · Physical Review C 110, 054609 (2024)

Inferring nuclear resonance properties from scattering data with quantified uncertainties.

Research summary by AI +

A Transformer-based probabilistic framework extracts resonance parameters directly from scattering data. Deep ensembles provide statistically calibrated uncertainties, while the training approach can bypass extraneous parameters that complicate phenomenological analysis.

Deep learning for experimental data

Restoring original signals from pile-up using deep learning

C. H. Kim et al. · Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research A 1055, 168492 (2023)

Recovering particle signal waveforms that overlap with unwanted signals.

Research summary by AI +

A one-dimensional convolutional neural network reconstructs original waveforms from pile-up in the Texas Active Target detector. Replacing distorted signals with reconstructed waveforms improves energy and timing information, particle identification, and particle tracks.

First author

Nuclear astrophysics

Estimation of the NiCu Cycle Strength and Its Impact on Type I X-Ray Bursts

C. H. Kim et al. · The Astrophysical Journal 929, 96 (2022)

Estimation of uncertain nuclear reaction rates to investigate the behavior of thermonuclear X-ray bursts.

Research summary by AI +

Nuclear data and Monte Carlo calculations constrain the competing copper-59 proton-capture and proton–alpha reaction rates. The resulting rates favor a weaker NiCu cycle; MESA simulations assess the effects on burst light curves and synthesized abundances.

Experimental nuclear astrophysics

Proton branching ratios of ²³Mg levels

C. H. Kim et al. · Physical Review C 105, 025801 (2022)

Experimental constraints on nuclear states relevant to Na-22 destruction in stellar explosions.

Research summary by AI +

Particle decays following the ²⁴Mg(p,d)²³Mg transfer reaction provide proton branching ratios for several excited states. These measurements support an improved high-temperature ²²Na(p,γ)²³Mg reaction rate, relevant to neon isotope anomalies in presolar grains.

03 About

AI, physical insight,
and scientific discovery.

I’m Chanhee (Ben) Kim, a researcher with a Ph.D. in physics. I develop AI and deep learning methods for physics, with a focus on nuclear physics and astrophysics. My work combines physical modeling, computational methods, and data-driven inference.

I’m particularly interested in interpretable AI, reliable extrapolation, uncertainty quantification, and agentic AI for scientific discovery. I believe deep learning can help us answer fundamental questions about how the universe works.

I also welcome opportunities to apply deep learning to questions in other areas of physics. If you’d like to discuss an idea, explore a collaboration, or request code from one of my studies, please get in touch.

Current funding as PI / 2026–present
